description: Route-level bundle size budgets for authenticated Next.js pages. Budgets cover the First Load JS (shared chunks + page chunk) for each route segment. Values are in bytes. Measured values are filled by the post-build bundle analyzer and compared against the declared ceiling by the orchestrator. A null measured value means the route has not been profiled yet.

network.mobile: ~1.6 Mbps down, 750 Kbps up, 150ms RTT — close to Fast 3G+ (browser-driver.mjs hardcoded: 1,600,000/8 bytes/s down, 750,000/8 bytes/s up, 150ms latency)

cpu.mobile: 4x CPU slowdown (Chrome DevTools mid-tier mobile preset)

referenceProfile.notes: Measured with Lighthouse 12 in CI using the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Field data (CrUX) is the source of truth for production; lab data here is the gating proxy. The 100ms responsiveness rule (CLAUDE.md §12.2) is enforced by INP ≤ 200ms. Bundle byte measurements require pnpm build (production webpack output); the current .next is a Turbopack dev build which cannot be compared to these ceilings.

/mail.note: Mail shell — first-load budget is higher because DOMPurify (isomorphic-dompurify) is a non-trivial dependency; compose sheet, AI toolbar and inbox summary sheet are lazy-loaded via next/dynamic

/inbox.note: Home inbox — lightweight notification-style inbox; no external mail provider calls

/crm/inbox.note: CRM inbox — deals and contact conversations
